A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EUVS benchmark. Their text, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, added and removed content.

before.justification: v1 reports original rendering and depth evaluations, dynamic-scene and lighting experiments, and a traversal-count analysis.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and supplementary analyses and additionally reports VEGS FID results.

M1.justification: Neither version introduces a new synthesis algorithm, and the described NVS methods retain their architectures and procedures. The masking-tool revision concerns experimental preprocessing.

E1.justification: Both use nuPlan, Argoverse 2 and MARS, reporting 90,810 frames across 345 videos and 104 cases. Translation, rotation, combined-pose scenarios and the Setting 2 dynamic-scene evaluation remain; renaming levels as settings does not expand coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same nine NVS baselines, and the depth comparison retains the same five methods. GS-W and OmniRe remain in renumbered tables. The new FID table evaluates the already included VEGS.

E3.justification: Table 1 and the GS-W/OmniRe tables change their stated comparison from training/test to interpolation/extrapolation while retaining identical numbers. Section 4.1 also replaces SegFormer masking with Grounded-SAM-2 and adds FID. These substantially revise the reported protocol, without establishing reruns; v3 Appendix Figure IV still labels the corresponding charts as training/test results.

E4.justification: The representation, diffusion-prior, depth-prior, lighting, dynamic-scene and traversal-count analyses remain. Several move from Sections 4.3–4.4 into Appendices A–B. FID extends performance measurement without adding a distinct ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained plots introduce no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 Table 2 adds VEGS FID results, averaging 42.0 for interpolation and 95.7 for extrapolation. v1 Table 3's separate 3DGS interpolation/extrapolation results are removed. Shared rendering, depth, GS-W and OmniRe numerical scores remain unchanged despite revised condition labels.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. The FID addition supplies an empirical metric without introducing a mathematical definition or derivation.

C1.justification: Both claim the first EUVS benchmark combining multi-traversal, multi-agent and multi-camera data and conclude that existing methods generalize poorly under large viewpoint changes. The broader NVS wording in v3's abstract reflects the Gaussian-Splatting and NeRF scope already stated in v1.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges missing foreground evaluation in Settings 1 and 3 and the absence of separate observed/unseen-region analysis. It qualifies Gaussian-versus-NeRF tradeoffs by geometry accuracy and viewpoint shift, and replaces several increasing-difficulty interpretations with discussion of complementary evaluation settings.

D1.justification: v3 discloses 300+ hours of manual selection, 800+ hours of COLMAP processing, exclusion of lidar initialization and lighting-consistency curation. It removes the statement that GS-W extracts appearance features from both training and test images. Reported data/code availability changes from already released to release upon acceptance; actual online availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Heusel et al. FID reference and the Ravi et al. SAM 2 reference, while removing SegFormer. The broader related-work coverage and positioning of EUVS remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the narrative, moving baseline comparisons and much of the method discussion into Appendices A–B and creating separate Discussions and Conclusions, Limitations and Future Work sections. Dataset descriptions, result summaries and lighting discussion are rewritten or condensed, with levels renamed settings throughout.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 6 is split between v3's main Figure 6 and appendix Figure I; traversal Figures 7–8 move to appendix Figures II–III. Tables are added, removed, reordered and relabeled, and dataset-distribution charts are redrawn. This substantially reorganizes the displays while retaining most underlying visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful FID evidence, curation disclosures and explicit limitations. However, identical scores acquire interpolation labels while appendix charts retain training labels, the separate interpolation comparison disappears, and reproducibility disclosures and release claims become less informative. The PDFs do not resolve whether the relabeling corrects earlier reporting or misstates the evaluation, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
